avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Folic Acid (>5mg daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Ribavirin inhibits IMPDH, disrupting purine synthesis; excessive folate may unmask or worsen cytopenias through competing metabolic pathways
avoid_supplements.action: Limit folic acid supplementation to RDA levels (400mcg); monitor CBC closely if supplementation necessary

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce intracellular phosphorylation enzymes and reduce ribavirin bioavailability; also increases risk of hepatotoxicity in HCV patients
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; discontinue St. John's Wort before starting ribavirin therapy

caution_supplements.name: Iron Supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Ribavirin may impair hematopoiesis; iron supplementation could mask anemia development or interact with antiviral efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Use only if iron deficiency documented; monitor hemoglobin/hematocrit regularly

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin E (>400 IU daily)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate anticoagulant effects if patient on concurrent antivirals with bleeding risk; unclear synergistic effects on viral clearance
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for bleeding signs; maintain moderate dosing and inform all providers of use

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit Juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: While ribavirin is not CYP3A4-metabolized, grapefruit affects concurrent medications (protease inhibitors, immunosuppressants) used with ribavirin in combination therapy
avoid_foods.action: Avoid grapefruit products during entire ribavirin treatment course

caution_foods.name: High-purine foods (organ meats, shellfish, red meat)
caution_foods.mechanism: Ribavirin disrupts purine synthesis via IMPDH inhibition; excessive dietary purines may create metabolic imbalance and worsen cytopenias
caution_foods.action: Moderate purine intake; ensure balanced diet with adequate protein from varied sources

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Alcohol potentiates hepatotoxicity and may worsen teratogenic risk in HCV patients; impairs hematopoietic recovery
caution_foods.action: Counsel strict alcohol avoidance, particularly in HCV/HBV co-infection; reinforce teratogenicity warnings

monitoring_notes: Monitor CBC (hemoglobin, hematocrit, platelets, WBC) every 2-4 weeks due to ribavirin-induced hemolytic anemia and cytopenias; assess liver function and renal function baseline and periodically. Ribavirin has significant teratogenic potential—ensure effective contraception in all reproductive-age patients and partner assessment for male patients.
